defects.description: Image-left shoulder blade is drawn upside-down. She lies face down with her head at the bottom of the frame, and her arms leave the torso at the shoulder line (y ~0.47-0.50). The blade's spine/acromion edge sits on that line (lateral tip ~(0.29,0.49)), but the triangular body extends TOWARD the head, with its inferior angle at ~(0.37,0.63) beside the hairline. That lays the blade over the base of the neck and upper trapezius instead of the upper back. It should extend from the shoulder line away from the head (up the image, around the practitioner's hands), with the inferior angle pointing toward the feet.

Image-right shoulder blade repeats the error as a mirror image: acromion/spine on the shoulder line (lateral tip ~(0.71,0.49)), inferior angle pointing toward the head at ~(0.63,0.63). Both blades are flipped 180 degrees along the body axis and sit between the shoulders and the head. A chiropractor would see upside-down shoulder blades over the neck.

notes: The specific old defects are gone: no blade floating in the mid/lower back, no stretched blade or pointed spike, no stray humerus to the table edge. But the shoulder blades are still misplaced, now as a symmetric pair flipped toward the head, so the overlay fails for the same structures. The spine is correct: a straight midline column of spinous processes from under the hands (y ~0.45) to the hairline (~0.72). The red glow sits around the upper spine between the drawn blades, from the hands toward the base of the neck, which matches the brief. Hands: two stacked hands, 9 digits visible, none extra, each joined to its own forearm. Patient arms hang continuously off both table sides to the bottom corners (elbows ~0.85); her hands are out of frame and her legs under the towel. Top edge is shirt chest only, no practitioner face. The console at right is blurred with no readable text.
